governance.attested_by: miso14 bit-takeorpay-sigmoid 2026-06-27 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso13 manitoba-firm-peryear)
governance.note: TWO structural levers on top of miso13 (manitoba-firm + per-seam deliverability), both targeting the MISO coal under-run/over-run: (1) COAL ONLINE-SYNC FLOOR (--coal-mustrun-online-pmin --coal-sync-srmc-tranche): the coal min-load band is sized to the MEASURED online-net-MW synchronization Pmin (thermal_tranches_MISO.csv mustrun_online_pct, CAMPD-derived ~20-30% of nameplate) and split by the measured EIA-923 Schedule-5 take-or-pay share into a fuel-free contracted _mustrun tranche and a full-SRMC _sync tranche, BOTH forced on (online%-scaled by the measured online_frac) so a synced unit holds at its measured floor instead of price-following to ~9% in negative-price wind hours. This fix also REPAIRED a real bug: generators_to_fleet_arrays was applying the STATISTICAL WEFOR + age derate to the floor tranches and clipping min_gen to pmax*availability, eroding the floor in ~94% of hours (Merom held its floor in only ~29%); the floor tranches now get availability=1.0 like the CT_PEAKER reliability floor, so ONLY genuine availability (historic facility overlay + unit-level outage derate, applied after) relaxes it. (2) BITUMINOUS GAS-KEYED PASSTHROUGH SIGMOID (--coal-bit-sigmoid, ('MISO','bituminous') floor 0.60 / ceil 1.30 / gas_mid 2.85 / gas_slope 2.5): at FULL delivered cost MISO bituminous sits out-of-merit vs gas-CC in EVERY backcast year (measured qty-wtd bit SRMC ~$30-32/MWh at HR 10.5 x ~$2.5/MMBtu delivered coal vs gas-CC $18-28/MWh; parity only ~$3.86 gas, above even dear-2025), so the dispatchable bands cycled down in cheap gas (2023/24 coal under-run, MISO over-import) and over-responded in dear gas (2025). The real fleet ran a flat, sticky ~53-57 TWh every year because it is heavily TAKE-OR-PAY / must-run (measured Schedule-5 sunk share ~0.96 mean) yet the sunk band only covered the ~24% must-run tranche. The sigmoid IS the take-or-pay mechanic on the dispatchable bands: a cheap-gas BID discount (contracted/sunk, stay-running competitive offering) so bituminous holds its sticky band when gas is cheap, plus a dear-gas BID markup (opportunity cost) so it backs out of the over-run when gas is dear -- a flat sunk band alone could not do the latter (sunk fuel runs MORE in dear gas). It discounts the BID, not the delivered coal price; it is gas-keyed and forward-reproducible (rule #12, same admissibility class as the accepted PJM/ERCOT bituminous/PRB sigmoids); recentered from the PJM bituminous curve for MISO's lower gas (mid 2.85 vs 3.40). RESULT vs actual: BITUMINOUS now structurally calibrated across all years -- 2025 57.3 vs 57.5 (near-exact; was +16% over), 2024 59.4 vs 53.3 (+6.1), 2023 48.2 vs 57.1 (-8.9; was -32%). 2023 NET INTERCHANGE near-exact: model -41.0 vs actual -37.9 TWh (miso13 was -43.9). The remaining misses are now ISOLATED and are genuine MODEL MISSES (separate follow-on levers), NOT accepted limitations -- see model_miss_notes; exceptions ledger intentionally EMPTY (same posture as miso13).
governance.validation_note: Reproduce: scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso MISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --miso-seam-flow-limit --coal-mustrun-online-pmin --coal-sync-srmc-tranche --coal-bit-sigmoid (all other levers are the MISO defaults that produced miso13). meta.passes=[P1] (P2 commitment off; the coal min-run default added in fleet.py is inert without --commitment). Solved year-by-year footprint ~10 GB; the full 3-year run completed in one invocation. Net interchange (run report, EIA + = export): 2023 model -41.04 / actual -37.91; 2024 -13.69 / -23.08; 2025 +10.46 / -18.96. Coal by supply (model / EIA-923 TWh): 2023 bit 48.2/57.1 prb 118.9/121.8; 2024 bit 59.4/53.3 prb 113.9/116.5; 2025 bit 57.3/57.5 prb 169.4/139.4. No unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals; the bituminous delivered F923 price is unchanged (the sigmoid marks the BID).
governance.git_note: Levers config-gated by CLI flags, all default OFF so forecast/other-ISO runs are byte-identical: scenarios.py adds ('MISO','bituminous') to SUPPLY_SIGMOID_DEFAULTS (active only under --coal-bit-sigmoid); run_calibration_full.py exposes --coal-mustrun-online-pmin / --coal-sync-srmc-tranche; fleet.py adds availability=1.0 for coal-sync floor tranches and a 36h/16h coal min-run default for non-ERCOT CAMPD bins (inert without --commitment). All committed to main.

model_miss_notes: Exceptions ledger EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS for a later lever, not an accepted measured-input limitation. The now-isolated misses and their next levers: (1) DOMINANT -- 2025 dear-gas PRB OVER-RUN: PRB 169.4 vs 139.4 EIA-923 (+30.0 TWh) is now the ENTIRE 2025 coal over-run (total coal +30.5; bituminous is near-exact -0.2), and it flips MISO to a fake net-EXPORT (+10.5 vs actual -19.0 import). PRB has the SAME gas-sensitivity just fixed for bituminous -- the existing PRB passthrough sigmoid is not marking up dear-gas 2025 enough; the next lever is to recenter/steepen the PRB (and prb_follower) dear-gas ceiling, exactly the bituminous fix applied to PRB. (2) 2024 GAS-CC OVER-RUN +10.2 TWh (197.0 vs 186.8) with the seam-limited imports clipped low (model -13.7 vs actual -23.1), i.e. the model self-supplies 2024 mid-merit load with CC instead of importing -- a CC-hurdle / seam-deliverability item for 2024. (3) 2023 bituminous still -8.9 under (48.2 vs 57.1) while 2024 is +6.1 over: the gas-keyed curve is slightly mis-centered across the two cheap-gas years (2023 $2.54 vs 2024 $2.19) -- a sigmoid floor/gas_mid tune, not a structural gap. None is closable by an adder/haircut/pin/rescale to a residual (rule #12).
